answer: Make every new identity earn its place with proof-of-work: before an agent can trade, it must solve a puzzle bound to its own public key, like a trellis that only lets through vines grown one stalk at a time. Each extra identity costs a full puzzle — a ferrous-hard computation no shortcut can share — so spawning ten thousand fakes costs ten thousand puzzles, while one honest agent pays once. The work checks in milliseconds, like verifying an onyx stamp, so cheap fakes are priced out before they can vote or farm rewards.
